name: Classical?
description: Given an array $$$a$$$, consisting of $$$n$$$ integers, find: $$$$$$\max\limits_{1 \le i \lt j \le n} LCM(a_i,a_j),$$$$$$ where $$$LCM(x, y)$$$ is the smallest positive integer that is divisible by both $$$x$$$ and $$$y$$$. For example, $$$LCM(6, 8) = 24$$$, $$$LCM(4, 12) = 12$$$, $$$LCM(2, 3) = 6$$$.
input_specification: The first line contains an integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 10^5$$$) — the number of elements in the array $$$a$$$. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^5$$$) — the elements of the array $$$a$$$.
output_specification: Print one integer, the maximum value of the least common multiple of two elements in the array $$$a$$$.
approach_summary: Precompute factorials and inverse factorials up to N using Fermat's Little Theorem (mod 10^9+7 or 998244353). Answer nCr queries in O(1) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1285F — Classical? [310. Large Factorials and Binomial Coefficients]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Combinatorial selection $\binom{N}{K} = \frac{N!}{K!(N-K)!} \pmod P$ can be evaluated in $O(1)$ by precomputing factorials $fact[i] = fact[i-1] \cdot i \pmod P$ and inverse factorials $invFact[i] = invFact[i+1] \cdot (i+1) \pmod P$ using Fermat's Little Theorem $a^{P-2} \equiv a^{-1} \pmod P$.
